title: Direct and constraints-led coaching

draft.title: Direct and constraints-led coaching
card: These see skill learning as a set path. The learner copies a correct technique and improves it step by step.
This approach suits linear theories. The coach shows the ideal technique, breaks the skill into parts, gives instructions and corrects errors.
These see skill learning as unique to each person. Each learner finds their own way to move, shaped by the task, the environment and their own body.
This approach suits non-linear theories. The coach changes the task, the environment or the rules, such as a smaller court or a lighter ball, so the learner finds their own solution.
draft.remember: Direct coaching tells the learner how to move. Constraints-led coaching shapes the setting so the learner finds how to move.

a.q: Which coaching method best fits a non-linear view of skill learning?
opts: Changing the court size so players find their own solutions
Showing one ideal technique for players to copy
Splitting the skill into parts and drilling each in turn
Correcting each error with a spoken instruction
a.why: A non-linear view says each learner finds their own way to move. Changing the task or environment lets that happen. The other options are direct coaching, where the coach sets the technique.
a.clue: Which option changes the setting rather than telling the player what to do?

b.q: Priya coaches junior netball. To help players learn to pass under pressure, she plays games with an extra defender and a shorter time limit, and gives no instructions on technique. Which approach is she using, and why?
opts: Constraints-led, because she changes the task and setting
Direct, because she controls the game and sets the rules
Constraints-led, because she gives no feedback to players
Direct, because she is working on one skill in a drill
b.why: Priya changes the task with an extra defender and a time limit, and leaves players to find their own solutions. That is constraints-led coaching. Setting rules does not make it direct, as direct coaching instructs the technique.
b.clue: Who decides how the pass is made: the coach or the players?

a.best: Changing the court size so players find their own solutions

b.best: Constraints-led, because she changes the task and setting
